title: asian shipbuilding dominance could thwart lng expansion wood mackenzie says 2026 07 08
text:
LONDON, July 8 (Reuters) - The biggest expansion of global ​LNG supply on record, led by the United States and ‌Qatar, could be slowed as most of the ships needed to transport the fuel are being built in South Korea and China, a Wood Mackenzie ​report said on Wednesday.
"The LNG industry talks constantly about energy ​security, diversification and resilience," Ikram Elloumi, director of research at Wood ⁠Mackenzie, said in the report. "Yet one of its most critical ​dependencies – the ability to physically move gas – rests on a supply chain ​it does not control and cannot quickly replicate."
